newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian vandals hit Florence's Neptune again.
newsitem.headline: Italian vandals hit Florence's Neptune again.

text.p: Vandals have attacked Florence's Neptune fountain, a jewel of the Italian Renaissance, for the second time this year, police said on Friday.
They said the hoof of one of the four horses that guard the marble Fountain of Neptune, carved by Ammannati in 1576, was found in the basin of the fountain.
Investigators believe vandals smashed it off with a hammer.
The statue has regularly been targeted by vandals in recent years and in January one of the horse's ears was snapped off.
In 1992, joyous supporters celebrated the victory of the Italian national team in soccer's World Cup by painting Neptune's shoulders blue.

The local council, which has its offices just metres (yards) from the fountain in the central Piazza della Signoria, installed eight remote control television cameras last year to try to deter would-be vandals.
However the cameras' field of vision has been blocked in recent months by scaffolding placed around a nearby building.
